title: Slice Variance Resilience Lab Notebook (WIP)
content:
Purpose
----
This is a working lab notebook for defining and iterating on a set of operational patterns aimed at making canary/A-B rollouts robust to slice-level variance. Goal is to provide cross-functional playbooks that help product, eng, SRE and CS teams detect, contain, and recover from localized instability (telemetry spikes, quality regressions, latency bursts) without full rollback.

Context / Motivation
----
We've seen multiple incidents where overall metrics looked stable, but a small cohort of users (a slice) experienced a sharp drop in quality or latency regressions that then cascaded (caching churn, routing flaps). Current runbooks are oriented to global signals and full-feature rollbacks. Need patterns for:
- early detection at slice granularity
- containment strategies that reduce blast radius while preserving experiment validity
- automated rescue sequences with human-in-loop thresholds

Key hypotheses (for validation)
----
1) Adding a small set of slice-specific sentinel signals (prefix-match lat p99, semantic drift score, token-penalty rate) will surface issues 30-60 minutes earlier than global aggregates.
2) Providing an automated slice-eviction pathway (traffic move to fallback model/version for that slice) reduces mean-time-to-repair vs full rollback without materially biasing experiment results if the evicted slice is small (<3% of traffic).
3) Lightweight synthetic probes mirrored from production prompts will reproduce slice degradation with >70% fidelity, allowing pre-mitigation rehearsal.

Experiment surface (sketch)
----
Matrix of experiments we should run in a staging environment first, then gradual production:
- Canary variant A vs baseline: instrument slice-level p50/p95/p99 latency, prompt-sim success, content-safety flags.
- Canary with slice-eviction enabled: automatically shift affected cohorts to fallback model instance. Measure recovery time and integrity of metric reporting.
- Canary + synthetic probing: run synthetic probes against both control and variant every 5m; correlate probe failure with user-observed degradation.

Signal design (practical)
----
Minimal sentinel signals (must be instrumented):
- Slice p99 latency (observed client-side, if available)
- Token-generation time per 100 tokens
- Response truncation rate (server-side)
- Semantic-consistency score (embedding drift from baseline for canonical prompts)
- Safety flag rate (content-moderation triggers per 1k responses)
- Routing/fallback count (how many requests triggered fallback)
Signal heuristics:
- Alert if slice p99 > baseline p99 * 1.5 AND safety-flag-rate increased by > 2x over 30m window
- Probe fail correlation: if synthetic probes for slice degrade and are correlated (Pearson r>0.6) with traffic signals, escalate to oncall.

Containment patterns (catalog)
----
1) Soft Quarantine (automated, immediate): reduce experiment exposure weight for the slice by 50% and route remainder to baseline. Keep experiment open, mark slice as under observation.
2) Slice Eviction (automated + reversible): move slice traffic to a predetermined fallback model/version; tag events in telemetry for downstream analysis.
3) Traffic Throttle + Probe-Only Mode (manual/automatic): pause external traffic, run high frequency probes to validate hypotheses before resuming.
4) Human Gate: if containment does not reduce adverse signals within N minutes (configurable), page oncall and product owner.

Rescue playbook (step-by-step)
----
When slice sentinel triggers fire:
- T0 (0-5m): Auto soft-quarantine kicks in, create an ops-annotation in the rollout ledger (console event). Notify Slack #rollouts-alerts with slice id, reason, snapshot of signals.
- T+5m: Recompute correlation with synthetic probes. If probe correlation high, trigger slice eviction to fallback model. Record routing decision.
- T+15m: If metrics trending back toward baseline, initiate controlled re-introduction: 10% bump over 30m windows while monitoring.
- T+30m: If metrics remain degraded, escalate to full rollback and trigger postmortem cadence.

Runbook snippets for SRE/Oncall
----
- Quick look commands (stubs):
  - ./rb query-slice-metrics --slice=<slice_id> --window=1h
  - ./rb show-routing --slice=<slice_id>
  - ./rb set-exposure --slice=<slice_id> --weight=0.5 --reason="auto-quarantine"
- Quick checklist:
  - confirm slice definition (cohort vs heuristics)
  - verify probe reproducibility
  - check per-model resource usage (GPU/queue backs)
  - decide containment vs rollback with product lead

Telemetry and observability needs (actionable)
----
Must-haves:
- slice_id persisted across logs/traces/metrics/alerts
- ability to graph slice-trajectories vs global baseline (time series overlays)
- synthetic-probe dashboard with per-probe failure reasons and heatmaps
- exposure ledger (audit log) that records containment actions and actors
Nice-to-haves:
- causal-attribution hints (why did latency spike: KV cache miss, kernel selection fallback, model OOM?)
- automated RCA links created when an incident transitions to postmortem

Human processes & communication templates
----
- Slack alert template (auto-populated):
  "[Auto-Quarantine] slice=<id> weight=0.5 reason=<signals> probe_corr=<value> owner=<team>"
- Post-quarantine swimlane: owner posts 1) what was observed, 2) containment action, 3) expected next step, 4) re-introduction criteria.
- Decision rubric for rollback vs containment: severity of user-facing harm, time to mitigate, number of affected slices, revenue impact estimate (from CS).

Open questions / unknowns
----
- How to reliably define slices that are stable across time? Current cohorting by country or user-agent drifts quickly. Need to experiment with multi-dim slicing (feature flags + behavior+geography).
- Probe fidelity: what fraction of user prompts do we need to include in synthetic set to hit 70% fidelity? Is privacy OK? (ask Legal)
- Does slice-eviction introduce bias into A/B results if not accounted for in analysis? Need stats team involvement to ensure valid inference.

Next steps (concrete)
----
- (Ava) Draft telemetry schema for slice_id and sentinel signals (due 2025-01-20).
- (Ravi) Prototype synthetic probe harness and run 24h shadow against staging variants (due 2025-01-28).
- (Elise) Stat/analysis writeup on how to adjust A/B inference for slice-evictions (due 2025-02-04).
- (Tom) Hook soft-quarantine into rollout console and add audit event (PR stub created: GITHUB:pr/789).

Appendix: quick glossary
----
- slice: a traffic cohort defined by attributes (country, user-tier, app-version, feature-flag).
- soft-quarantine: automated exposure weight reduction designed to slow blow-ups while preserving signal.
- slice-eviction: routing action that sends affected slice to a fallback model/version.
- probe: synthetic request constructed from production prompt templates to validate model behavior.

Notes to self (scratchpad)
----
- check with Legal on probe prompt retention window and hashing.
- build small training deck for CS on interpreting slice dashboards.
- run tabletop next week (w/ product, SRE, solutions eng) to rehearse quarantine->eviction flow.

End of notebook entry (WIP)
